story.subtitle: Express Yourself
story.content: I was born with a great passion for visual arts. I watched every cartoon on TV and was happiest with a crayon in my hand. My parents thought I had a talent for art, so they signed me up for private lessons with art teachers who expanded my mind.
story.alt: A kid drawing on the wall

story.subtitle: Wild Thing
story.content: My father brought home a brand-new Commodore 64 and I was stunned. I mostly played video games, but one day I found a 5¼-inch floppy disk with a program that made amazing greeting cards. Soon I was making big banners with Bannermania and printing them on an old dot-matrix printer.

story.subtitle: Modern Love
story.content: When I saw the Web for the first time, I wanted to be part of it. I spent long hours on my dial-up connection learning about webmasters and web design. Geocities, Lycos and Freeservers showed me the way. I made my first website, “Otto’s”, with FrontPage and a bunch of stolen GIFs.

story.subtitle: Money for Nothing
story.content: While I was finishing high school, a friend showed me Photoshop 5.0 and how to manipulate photos. I made some money removing scratches from old family pictures and colorizing black-and-white photos. I realized it was a really fun gig and that I could make a career out of it.

story.subtitle: All Day and All of the Night
story.content: I started working as a junior designer while I was studying Graphic Design at university. Back then, schools were outdated and there was no Web or Multimedia Design degree. I was hungry for knowledge, so I learned Web Design all day and Design Fundamentals all night.
story.alt: A young man juggling Flash, academy and money balls

story.subtitle: Comfortably Numb
story.content: After 10 years as a web designer, I felt stuck. I had a good job with great benefits, but the rate of change outside exceeded the rate of change inside: inside the company and inside myself. The end was near, and I had to do something.
story.alt: Overweight man working with a computer

story.subtitle: Wake Up
story.content: I quit my job and became an avid learner again. I worked as a freelancer while I improved my motion graphics skills, explored design software beyond the Adobe universe, and researched new trends in design and user experience.

story.subtitle: Are You Experienced?
story.content: I signed up for a year-long course on Accessibility and User Experience at UTN. It helped me step away from the keyboard and learn from users and colleagues. Design is no longer a designer in front of a computer. It’s a whole team working with clients and users to build a great product.

story.subtitle: Extra bonus!
story.alt: Man painting a mobile phone like a canvas
story.content: COVID shifted my career path toward the place where all my passions meet: design, illustration, animation and technology. Today I create the art and interactive experiences for mobile games that people play every day.

story.title: Today
story.subtitle: New Sensation
story.content: I am always looking for new opportunities that could make me a better designer. If you think you have the perfect challenge for me, drop me a line.
story.alt: Bearded man writing at a desk
